liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Jam** (3 reviews): Unique Jam begins minutes into a rough Truckin', with Garcia bending notes like Santana while Phil roams; The jam between Truckin' and Dark Star makes the show worth the effort [7][8][9]
- **Dark Star** (3 reviews): Dark Star emerges gradually from the Jam with the intro skipped; its destination is unclear until about eight minutes in; Reviewer finds this deep-space Dark Star unlike any other, a time-travel experience [6][11][12]
- **Box of Rain** (2 reviews): Reviewer calls Box of Rain very good, a standout among the show's songs; Reviewer calls this probably the best Box of Rain from the period, with tasty Garcia licks [4][8]
- **The Promised Land** (1 review): Promised Land is cut; the tape joins at the slow final solo [15]
- **Sugaree** (1 review): Sugaree is slow and sultry, sounding more country than psychedelic [15]
- **Playin' in the Band** (1 review): Eighteen-minute Playin' alternates Garcia's edgy themes with shimmering rushes from Weir and Keith [7]
- **Morning Dew** (1 review): Truckin' into Dark Star into Morning Dew is called brilliant for fans of 1972 jamming [6]

## The recordings

- **gd72-12-15.sbd.hollister.17186.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 26 songs; 188 min; rated 4.33/5 by 12 [1]. Said about its sound: The opening set of this soundboard has many spliced tracks; Sound is pretty good, with a couple of glitches; Reviewer hears hiss and rates the quality A [4][5][6][8]
- **gd1972-12-15.sbd.yerys.2329.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 26 songs; 193 min; rated 3.62/5 by 8 [2]. Said about its sound: Soundboard has a little hiss, and the vocals sit slightly high in the mix; Early on, Weir's vocals are low and Phil is inaudible; the balance is corrected by Sugaree's end [7][15]
- **gd1972-12-15.136651.sbd.reel1.dat.sirmick.flac16**: soundboard; 27 songs; 188 min; rated 2.6/5 by 5 [3]

## Around the show

- Attendee sat with about twenty friends on the stage-left risers; they shared wine spiked with LSD before Candyman [10]
- Reviewer says many 1972 shows are better than this one [5]
- Reviewer feels the show sounds like it sits between 1972 and 1973 [9]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd72-12-15.sbd.hollister.17186.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Remastered, transferred to CD, and encoded to SHN by David Hollister; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Lineage runs from a master reel through cassette and DAT to CD, patched from another reel copy; Hollister remastered and encoded it [1]
- **gd1972-12-15.sbd.yerys.2329.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Unknown; transferred by Ben Yerys; source: SBD > Master Reel [2]. Also: Per Tiedrich's site, the master reel's speed was off for Truckin', so that portion was edited out [2]
- **gd1972-12-15.136651.sbd.reel1.dat.sirmick.flac16**: taped by Anonomous; transferred by SIRMick; source: Source: Soundboard > Master-Reel > Reel (1st gen) > DAT [3]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Long Beach Arena - December 15, 1972](https://www.dead.net/show/december-15-1972) [17]
